title: Scalar mates for the standard affine-line compactification
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. All schemes and morphisms are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings and let $N=\ell^n\geq1$ annihilate both. On small ordinary etale sites use the constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $\mathcal C_{T,R}=D^b_{ctf}(T_{et},R)$ for the full subcategory of complexes with bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude, meaning that derived tensor with every degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology in one fixed finite interval [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer]. Put $T_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $R_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$, and $R_T(d)=R_T(1)^{\otimes d}$ for $d\geq0$, with $R_T(0)=R_T$ [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line].
Let $T$ be such a base and let $j:U=\mathbf A^1_T\hookrightarrow P=\mathbf P^1_T$, $q:P\to T$ be the standard chart and projection [def-amb-affine-trace-tower]. Restrict to $\mathcal C_{-,R}$ the adjunctions $J_R=Dj_!\dashv H_R=j^*$, with sum/evaluation counit $v_R$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension, lem-sp-etale-sum-counit-scalar], and $Q_R=Rq_{*,R}\dashv V_R=q^*(-)(1)[2]$, with the normalized projective-line counit $w_R$ [lem-sp-p1-counit-scalar]. Use the actual composite adjunction $L_R=Q_RJ_R\dashv W_R=H_RV_R$, whose counit is $e_R=w_R\circ Q_R(v_RV_R)$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Let $s:T_PJ_A\xrightarrow{\sim}J_BT_U$ be the summandwise tensor map and $b:T_TQ_A\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_BT_P$ the proper coefficient map [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. Let $h:T_UH_A\xrightarrow{\sim}H_BT_P$ and $a:T_PV_A\xrightarrow{\sim}V_BT_T$ be the canonical derived tensor/pullback, Tate and shift comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Set
$$b^u=Q_B(s)\circ bJ_A:T_TL_A\xrightarrow{\sim}L_BT_U,\qquad a^u=H_B(a)\circ hV_A:T_UW_A\xrightarrow{\sim}W_BT_T.$$
Then $b^u$ is the coefficient map of the standard compactification $(j,q)$, and $a^u$ is the mate of $(b^u)^{-1}$ for these actual composite adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. For every $K\in\mathcal C_{T,A}$,
$$e_{B,T_TK}\circ L_B(a^u_K)\circ b^u(W_AK)=T_T(e_{A,K}).$$
All displayed maps are restricted to the stated finite-Tor subcategories; no flatness or finite projective dimension of $B$ over $A$ is assumed.

source.place: Charts: Scalar mates for the standard affine-line compactification; retained affine-counit proof steps 2, 3

proof.text: By [lem-sp-etale-ctf-chart-domain], all functors in the question preserve the indicated finite-Tor subcategories: apply its compact-support assertion to $j$ and to $q$ (using identity proper/open factors respectively), and its pullback/twist/shift assertion to $H_R$ and $V_R$. In particular $V_AK$, $H_AV_AK$ and their scalar extensions are valid inputs to the comparisons below. The standard open chart is separated etale of finite type and $q$ is proper. By [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility], the coefficient map for this chosen compactification is, by definition, the proper coefficient map followed by the extension-by-zero tensor identification. The first factor is $bJ_A$. For the second, $j$ is an open immersion, so its sum extension is extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension]: at most one lift indexes each summand. Apply the last displayed identity of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] to $e=j$ with the compactification $(j,1_P)$. Its proper factor is the transpose of the identity counit, hence the identity, and $c_{j,R}$ is the canonical identification $R1_{P*}Dj_!\simeq Dj_{\Sigma!}$. So the extension-by-zero tensor identification is the summandwise map $s$, and $Q_B$ of it is $Q_B(s)$. Thus the composite is $b^u$. Each factor is an isomorphism on the stated inputs. No identification with a different compactification is used.

source.place: Charts, iterated projective-line integration; affine-line scalar mates, step 1

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sp-etale-sum-counit-scalar] to $e=j$ and to the object $V_AK\in\mathcal C_{P,A}$. Its maps $\sigma_e$ and $a_e$ are precisely $s$ and $h$ of the question. Thus
$$v_{B,T_PV_AK}\circ J_B(h_{V_AK})\circ s_{H_AV_AK}=T_P(v_{A,V_AK}).$$
This is the open-adjunction identity at the required, twisted and shifted, input.

source.place: Charts, iterated projective-line integration; affine-line scalar mates, step 2

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sp-p1-counit-scalar] with base $T$. Its $F_R,G_R,\epsilon_R,\beta_q$ are the stipulated $Q_R,V_R,w_R,b$, with exactly the prescribed projective-line normalization. Its canonical right comparison is $a_K$. Hence
$$w_{B,T_TK}\circ Q_B(a_K)\circ b_{V_AK}=T_T(w_{A,K}).$$

source.place: Charts, iterated projective-line integration; affine-line scalar mates, step 3

proof.text:
Write $v=v_{A,V_AK}$, $v'=v_{B,T_PV_AK}$ and $w'=w_{B,T_TK}$. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] the actual composite counit is $e_R=w_R\circ Q_R(v_RV_R)$. Naturality of $v_B$ at $a_K:T_PV_AK\to V_BT_TK$ gives
$$v_{B,V_BT_TK}\circ J_BH_B(a_K)=a_K\circ v'.$$
Expand $a^u$, $b^u$ and $e_B$ in the left side of the desired equation and use this equality. It becomes
$$w'\circ Q_B(a_K)\circ Q_B\bigl(v'\circ J_B(h_{V_AK})\circ s_{H_AV_AK}\bigr)\circ b_{J_AH_AV_AK}.$$
Step 2 replaces the parenthesized map by $T_P(v)$. Naturality of $b:T_TQ_A\to Q_BT_P$ at $v:J_AH_AV_AK\to V_AK$ says
$$Q_B(T_P(v))\circ b_{J_AH_AV_AK}=b_{V_AK}\circ T_T(Q_A(v)).$$
The expression is therefore $w'\circ Q_B(a_K)\circ b_{V_AK}\circ T_T(Q_A(v))$. Step 3 makes this
$$T_T(w_{A,K})\circ T_T(Q_A(v))=T_T(e_{A,K}),$$
by functoriality and the same composite-counit formula. All products are composition, with the rightmost map applied first.

source.place: Charts, iterated projective-line integration; affine-line scalar mates, step 4

proof.text:
The composite $b^u$ is invertible by step 1. Precomposing the equation proved in step 4 with $(b^u_{W_AK})^{-1}$ gives
$$e_{B,T_TK}\circ L_B(a^u_K)=T_T(e_{A,K})\circ(b^u_{W_AK})^{-1}.$$
By the transpose characterization in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], this says precisely that $a^u$ is the mate of $(b^u)^{-1}$ for $L_A\dashv W_A$ and $L_B\dashv W_B$, with coefficient functors $T_U,T_T$. Naturality follows from the given natural comparisons $a,h$, so the component calculation proves the assertion for natural transformations. All steps took place in $D^b_{ctf}$ and used derived tensor; none supposes that coefficient extension preserves every bounded-below complex.
